1ln3e7u: «Llevar» + amount of time + gerund measures an action from when it began up to the moment you are talking about: «llevamos ocho meses lijando el casco». It works in the present, the imperfect and the future: «llevaba dos años trabajando en Castro cuando la conoció», «en abril llevaré un año viviendo aquí». It isn't used in the preterite; for a closed duration say «estuve dos años viviendo en Castro» or «viví dos años en Castro».
1a0w48f: If what you are measuring is time without doing something, use «llevar» + time + «sin» + infinitive: «lleva tres semanas sin venir al astillero». And with a place or a state no gerund is needed: «lleva un año en Puerto Montt», «llevo una semana resfriado». Pronouns can go before «llevar» or attached to the gerund: «lo llevamos pintando dos días» or «llevamos dos días pintándolo».
dk1f3l: Before using «llevar», ask yourself whether the action is still open at the moment you are talking about. If it has finished, change the verb.

115xhjb: «Ir» + gerund presents gradual, step-by-step progress: «el casco va tomando forma», «ve preparando las herramientas mientras llego» (start and keep going). «Venir» + gerund looks from a point in the past up to today and usually indicates that something is repeated or insisted on: «la cooperativa viene pidiendo un muelle nuevo desde 2019». It is very common in the press.
3v8cpr: «Andar» + gerund is colloquial: it describes an activity done here and there, without order, and often carries criticism: «anda diciendo que la lancha no flotará». In Mexico and other areas it is used a lot and is usually neutral: «ando buscando trabajo».

Here we just put them in order so you can choose quickly. «Echarse a» and «romper a» mark a sudden start, especially with llorar, reír or correr: «se echó a reír», «rompió a llover». «Volver a» indicates repetition. «Estar a punto de» marks something imminent; «estar por» means the same in many parts of Latin America, and in others, to feel like doing something. «Acabar» + gerund and «terminar por» + infinitive tell the outcome after a process.

18s8skn: The future perfect is formed with the future of «haber» and the past participle: «habré terminado». Its main use is to place yourself at a future moment and look back: what will already be done by then? That reference point almost always appears: «para marzo», «antes de la regata», «cuando llegue el invierno», «dentro de un año». It is also used to take stock up to a future date: «cuando me jubile, habré construido cuarenta botes».
llnu7a: Without a future reference point, the same form is usually read as a guess about something that has already happened: «Tomás no contesta; habrá dejado el teléfono en el taller». It is a hypothesis, not a fact, so it's best to check it before acting.

ijz600: By the time this newsletter reaches your homes, the «Esperanza» will have turned sixty-two. She is a larch and oak boat that for decades carried shellfish from Chiloé to Puerto Montt, and which has been abandoned in a corner of the boatyard since 2015. This year, a group of members decided she wasn't going to rot there. Since March, every Saturday, the cooperative has been gathering volunteers to restore her.
1gq5bl2: The work is going at a slow pace. It is led by Rocío Aguilar, a wooden-boat builder who has been building and repairing vessels for forty years. «At first I thought it would be enough to change ten planks», she says. «We ended up changing forty-three». Each new plank has to be bent with steam, fitted and caulked by hand, with oakum and pitch, as it used to be done. Her nephew Tomás, an engineering student in Puerto Montt, hasn't missed a Saturday in eight months, although he admits that in July he was about to give up: «It rained three weekends in a row and you couldn't work».
txnjba: Not everything depends on the group. The original engine, a 1970 diesel, has been causing problems since day one. Don Aurelio Mancilla, who was the boat's last skipper, knows it better than anyone, but he hasn't shown up at the boatyard for weeks. «He must have had to take care of himself», they say on the pier, and nobody dares call him so as not to bother him. Meanwhile, a mechanic from Calbuco comes back to check it every fortnight.
7wmsi1: The deadlines are tight, but Rocío is clear about them. By the end of January they will have finished the bottom; in February they will paint the hull blue and white, the colours of the first owner; and before the regatta on 10 March they will have tested the engine in the bay. If all goes well, that day the «Esperanza» will leave the Angelmó pier with twelve volunteers on board.
1uxm1kj: And afterwards? Nobody has decided yet. Some propose using her for school trips; others, keeping her as a floating museum. What is clear is that, when they launch her, the cooperative will have recovered more than a boat: it will have brought three generations of the cove together again around the same work. If you want to help, on Saturdays from nine there's coffee, homemade bread and always a free piece of sandpaper.
